prompt:
Fella analytical answer output format: json-render spec fella-json-render-v1.
Author a nested tree: {"version":"fella-ui-1","intent":"trend","capabilities":["display"],"state":{},"root":{"type":"Document","children":[{"type":"Title","props":{"content":"Answer"}}]}}. The host generates element IDs, child references and empty leaf children. Use optional explicit id only to preserve identity across revisions.
Intent describes the user goal (lookup, comparison, trend, distribution, relationship, exploration, explanation), not a layout template. Choose components that clarify this question. A plain canonical answer without a presentation is valid; never add decorative interactivity.
Every analytical value binds to a supplied saved resultId and field. Metric and Progress also use a zero-based row. Chart encodings and Table fields reference only saved columns. No datasets, queries, code, network access, executable expressions or arbitrary chart transforms. Chart.spec must match its full typed schema, including supported layer, facet, repeat and concat forms.
For local controls declare state: {"view":{"type":"enum","options":[{"value":"chart","label":"Chart"},{"value":"table","label":"Exact values"}],"default":"chart","persistence":"viewer"}}. Boolean state uses type:boolean, default:boolean, persistence:viewer. Bind Select, SegmentedControl or Checkbox using bind:{state:"view"}; the host derives stateKey, options and defaults.
Every state must have a producer and a visible or filtering consumer. Conditional nodes use when:{state:"view",equals:"chart"}. Chart/Table filtering uses filters:[{state:"region",field:"region"}]. Filter enum values must match exact saved column values; the explicit $all choice means all saved rows. Filters are local saved-row display operations, not SQL or a model call. Defaults must be valid, modest, visible and reversible. Selections are viewer state; saved defaults and export snapshots retain explicit state.
Tabs need only TabPanel children with props.label and nested children; an explicit Tabs id preserves selection identity. Do not author labels arrays, panel names or indices; the host derives them. Keep tabs useful and accessible.
The display capability permits presentation and local state only. Declare follow_up as well only when including FollowUp or Button follow_up. Those actions require an explicit user click and remain subject to host policy. Scenario, query, code and network capabilities are not implemented; do not request them or imitate hypothetical values as observed evidence.
Use only registered components, props, bindings and typed chart settings. Host defaults provide Fella styling, spacing, sizing and routine formatting. Preserve coverage limitations and source caveats. Existing flat root/elements presentations are an internal compatibility format, not the preferred authoring language.
Shared resource limits: {"specBytes":256000,"components":240,"depth":24,"results":32,"rowsPerResult":10000,"cells":200000,"resultCharacters":8000000,"chartNodes":6000,"chartLayers":24,"chartPixels":8000000,"chartWork":500000,"numericFormatDigits":4,"jsonNodes":20000,"jsonDepth":128,"facets":60,"text":16000}. Chart strings cannot contain URL/resource schemes, url(...), or script/svg/iframe markup. Numeric format strings allow at most four consecutive digits to bound label allocations. Facet/repeat panels, composed pixels and row/view work are cumulative conservative budgets. Linked chart fields must be encoded as raw unaggregated values. Saved-row options must exist in their bound result. These semantic constraints are checked before acceptance.
Choose an answer-specific visual presentation from the question, verified answer, and supplied result shape. The model chooses the composition: concise prose, exact metrics, tables, charts, comparisons, or a useful combination. Do not repeat one layout for every question. Do not use a table merely because analysis returned rows. Use a visualization when it makes a trend, ranking, distribution, relationship, or comparison easier to understand; a table is best for exact records, lookups, and detail. Keep the answer readable, responsive, and free of redundant decoration.

Choose chart forms by the analytical task, not by a default template: when the user asks for a trend or change across three or more ordered time periods and the result has a numeric measure, make a chart the primary view unless that would mislead; line charts make observed values easy to compare, while area charts emphasize continuous volume or accumulated magnitude. Bars compare categories or rank values (use horizontal bars for long labels); pie or donut charts show a small, meaningful part-to-whole breakdown, not time trends or long rankings; points show relationships or distributions. Group, stack, facet, or layer only when it clarifies a real comparison and the scales remain interpretable. Other safe Vega-Lite compositions are welcome when they better fit the result. Use a tooltip for useful exact values, a legend only when it helps decode multiple series, and axis titles or captions for units and scope. Keep labels readable and avoid unnecessary precision. Do not imitate unsupported chart forms with custom executable expressions.

Use Fella's registered components and design. Prefer a clear reading order, consistent spacing and type hierarchy, restrained surfaces, accessible labels, the Fella chart-color palette, and responsive layouts. Avoid cramped equal-weight cards, horizontal overflow, decorative controls, and repeated content. Keep caveats near affected values. Never imply completeness when a supplied result is incomplete.

Registered components:
Document: The root analytical answer. Organize it into a useful reading order.
Author props: (none). Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Card: A restrained surface grouping related information. Use sparingly, not around every element.
Author props: title, detail, tone. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Section: A titled, left-aligned group of analytical content.
Author props: title. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Columns: A responsive group of at most three content columns; collapses at narrow widths.
Author props: count. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Row: A flexible horizontal group that wraps at narrow widths.
Author props: gap, align. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Grid: A responsive grid for a small set of related components.
Author props: columns. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Divider: A quiet separator between major content groups.
Author props: label. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Spacer: A small amount of intentional breathing room.
Author props: size. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Title: A clear heading for the answer or one of its major sections.
Author props: content, level. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Text: Explanatory prose with Markdown emphasis, lists, and links. Use structured Table and Chart components for analytical results.
Author props: content. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Caption: Quiet supporting context such as units, date range, source, or caveat.
Author props: content. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Badge: A compact label for a category or meaningful status.
Author props: content, tone. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Callout: An emphasized interpretation or caveat; not routine decoration.
Author props: title, content, tone. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Metric: A prominent exact value read from a supplied saved result. Always bind resultId, field and zero-based row; literal metric values are not accepted.
Author props: resultId, field, row, title, unit, format, detail. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Select: A local selector that changes only the presentation state, not the question or analysis.
Author props: name. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
SegmentedControl: A compact single-choice local presentation control for a few mutually exclusive options.
Author props: name. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Checkbox: A local display toggle; it does not change analytical definitions.
Author props: label. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Button: A deliberate user action. Its only allowed effect is to set local display state or ask Fella a follow-up.
Author props: label, action. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Table: A result-bound table for exact records, lookups, and detailed comparisons. For linked filtering, use the same interactionGroup on compatible components and include only visible raw fields in linkBy. Do not choose a table by default when a chart better explains a pattern.
Author props: resultId, fields, title, columnFormats, interactionGroup, linkBy. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Chart: A responsive result-bound Vega-Lite visualization with a typed declarative grammar: a unit mark with field encodings, nested layers with inherited parent encodings, a facet with a unit/layer spec, repeat with a child spec, or concat/hconcat/vconcat with child specs. Choose line or area for time trends, bars for comparisons, arcs for a small part-to-whole view, or points for relationships. Use static mark styles, axes, time units, scales, legends, and saved-field tooltips to clarify the answer. Keep labels, units, series and composed views readable. Data, loaders, expressions, transforms, params, and arbitrary config are forbidden. Author top-level filters bind declared local state to saved fields. For chart-click filtering, list displayed categorical fields in linkBy and use the same interactionGroup on compatible components. Authored display controls use saved rows only and do not replay queries.
Author props: resultId, spec, title, interactionGroup, linkBy. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Progress: A compact indicator for an exact saved numeric value bound to a result row.
Author props: resultId, field, row, title, maximum, detail. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
Tabs: A local presentation tab set. Supply TabPanel children; the host derives its name and labels.
Author props: (none). Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
TabPanel: One child panel of Tabs. Author props.label; the host derives the panel name and index.
Author props: label. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
ResultFilter: An exact-value selector sourced from rows in a saved result. Give it an interactionGroup to link it to compatible components that expose the same field. Authored display controls are limited to saved rows; no query is replayed. This control never asks the model to query or changes source scope.
Author props: resultId, field, name, title, interactionGroup. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.
FollowUp: An explicit user-pressed follow-up request to Fella.
Author props: label, message. Full types are in the supplied authoring schema.

Available result bindings (metadata only; the result rows themselves are provided separately as evidence):
[]
